summary: Billerica, MA stone building on Maryknoll/St. Vincent Seminary grounds, used as a lookout in 1938-39 after the Chelmsford tower fell to the hurricane; still standing and privately owned in 2018.

facts.design: existing stone structure, not built as a lookout; pressed into fire tower use in 1938
facts.status_note: Register says it still stood in 2015; a 2018 chapter post says it still stands. No newer source found

access.note: Privately owned per register (2015) and chapter post (2018); no public access described

events.note: State opened the tower in October 1938 and named Arthur R. Hallenborg observer (Lowell Sun item dated October 10, 1938)
Observer reported six fires the day before the October 10, 1938 item
Chelmsford's steel tower was destroyed by the 1938 hurricane; this stone structure was pressed into service in its place
Register and 2015 blog say it was used until Chelmsford's tower was rebuilt in 1939; a 2018 chapter post says it was used briefly in 1938
Added to the Former Fire Lookout Sites register August 30, 2015; nominated by Henry Isenberg
Chapter post says the structure still stands, privately owned, and is used as a horse barn

corrections.why: Register says the stone structure still stood in 2015, and a 2018 chapter post says it still stands, privately owned, used as a horse barn. The lookout use ended in 1938 or 1939, but the structure itself is not recorded as gone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register spells it Billeria; the town is Billerica, which the 2015 blog, the 2018 chapter post and the 1938 Lowell Sun item use. The story uses the town spelling and the record name is left as registered.

The 1938 Lowell Sun item confirms the state opened the tower in October 1938. The end of use conflicts: the register and 2015 blog say until Chelmsford's tower was rebuilt in 1939, while the 2018 chapter post says briefly in 1938. The story reports both and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: Status correction: the brief's 'gone' contradicts the register (2015) and the 2018 chapter post, both of which say the stone structure still stands. No source newer than 2018 was found, so current condition is unconfirmed. Use period conflicts (1939 vs briefly in 1938) are unresolved and both are reported. The build date of the stone structure is not in any source read, so no built event is recorded. The Lowell Sun text comes through a compilation site (easternuslookouts.weebly.com), not the original newspaper. The horse-barn and horse-paddock details are from a chapter post and a personal blog, so treat them as reports, not checked facts.
